judged_text: The connection getter now unconditionally POSTs to Salesforce's token endpoint and writes the credential row on every service construction — no expiry check, no timeout — where previously jsforce refreshed lazily only when the stored token expired. Every Salesforce-connected booking operation gains a remote token refresh plus a DB write (token churn and rate-limit exposure), and a transient token-endpoint failure or network blip now fails operations that would previously have succeeded with the still-valid stored access token.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, new code unconditionally calls `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and then `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning a `jsforce.Connection`, with no check of whether the existing `credential.key.access_token` is still valid/expired and no explicit request timeout. That is a concrete behavior/perf/reliability regression grounded in the diff (extra remote call + DB write per service construction, and operations can now fail on transient token-endpoint/network errors even if the stored token could have been used). However, whether this happens on “every booking operation” depends on higher-level lifecycle not shown in the diff, so it’s better framed as an important architectural concern rather than a strictly provable functional defect from the diff alone.
